In a large public school, $34$ students were surveyed about their weekend habits. For each student, the average time spent doing homework on Saturdays ($x$, in hours) and the average time spent streaming shows on Saturdays ($y$, in hours) were recorded to the nearest half hour. The scatter plot above shows the data with a line of best fit.

The line of best fit **underestimates** one student’s reported streaming time by more than $1.5$ hours. For how many hours did this student report doing homework on Saturdays?

![](images/c6/c6211ffc8fcf297e7181fdc364d5f2c4f3c032f3e33d4b507de907d152fa1219.png)

A neighborhood book club surveyed $36$ members. For each member, the average time spent reading on a typical day ($x$, in hours) and the average time spent discussing books ($y$, in hours) were recorded to the nearest half hour. The scatter plot above shows the data with a line of best fit.

The line of best fit **overestimates** one member’s reported discussion time by more than $1.5$ hours. How many hours did this member report reading?

:knowledge-point/title: Identifying the Worst Predicted Data Point
